quarterly_data.signal: Q2 revenue in line with guidance, nearly doubling sequentially as the photonics production ramp gathered pace; equipment revenue mix: 54% optoelectronics, 23% LED and Micro LED, 22% GaN and SiC power, 2% R&D tools; operating cash flow EUR 119 million and free cash flow EUR 114 million in Q2 on strong customer advance payments
quarterly_data.figure: revenue EUR 115 million, up from EUR 59 million in Q1, down 16% YoY; gross margin 41%; EBIT EUR 15 million (13% margin)

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 guidance confirmed with a steep quarter-over-quarter output ramp; Q4 targeted above the Q3 level and Q1 2027 expected to be strong, probably around the Q4 2026 level; gross margin expected to see a clear uptick in 2027 on laser system mix and fixed cost absorption
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue EUR 560 million ±EUR 30 million, gross margin about 42%, EBIT margin between 17% and 20%; Q3 revenue EUR 180 million ±EUR 20 million

quarterly_data.signal: Strong new orders predominantly driven by optoelectronics — 75% of Q2 equipment orders; the key driver is the architectural shift in AI data centers from copper towards high speed optical connectivity at 800G and eventually 1.6T and beyond; a diversified set of almost 15 laser companies makes up about 80% of order intake, from Europe, the U.S., Taiwan, Japan and China; around EUR 200 million quarterly order intake expected for the coming quarters
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 orders EUR 215 million; ~EUR 200 million quarterly order intake expected going forward

quarterly_data.signal: The limiting factor is ramp rate, not capacity — how fast AIXTRON and its suppliers can hire and train people; output ramping 3X within the year (EUR 59 million Q1 to over EUR 200 million implied in Q4); customer advance payments fund the ramp
quarterly_data.figure: advance payments EUR 197 million at end of June, around 43% of the equipment order backlog, more than EUR 150 million above year-end 2025

quarterly_data.signal: Customers are increasingly standardizing on the G10-AsP platform for advanced photonic devices (yield, uniformity, cost of ownership); near-term demand driven by indium phosphide EMLs and CW lasers for data centers, with customers already working on photonic integrated circuits (PICs) as the next step; roughly 70%-80% of systems ship configured for 4-inch wafers, prepared for 6-inch conversion; initial 80-120 tools per year opto market view now seeing stronger momentum than that

Power electronics stable at a low level: SiC installed base underutilized, GaN utilization around 60%-70% and gradually increasing; GaN has a strong opportunity in AI data centers for 800-volt DC to DC conversion, with SiC coming first at the high-voltage entry point and GaN following with a delay; mid-term view of a GaN market 3X-ing to around EUR 450 million of tool revenue fully holds; AIXTRON systems (G5+ and G10-GaN) are the tools of record across the GaN power market, so customers are expected to arrive with multi-dozen tool orders when the wave starts
quarterly_data.figure: GaN installed-base utilization around 60%-70%; mid-term GaN tool revenue view around EUR 450 million

quarterly_data.signal: Construction of the new Penang, Malaysia site has started and is fully on track; full-year CapEx of around EUR 55 million includes approximately two-thirds of the announced EUR 40 million Malaysia investment; liquidity EUR 816 million at June 30
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 CapEx around EUR 55 million, Malaysia investment EUR 40 million
